forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

statement_nl: Let a, b, and r be integers with 0 <= a < b and r >= 0. Define the graded polynomial ring Lambda_b := Q[e_1,...,e_b] with deg(e_i) = i, let R_{a,b} := Lambda_b/(e_1,...,e_a), and define elements h_t in Lambda_b by (sum_{i=0}^b (-1)^i e_i z^i)(sum_{t>=0} h_t z^t) = 1, where e_0 := 1. Let bar h_t be the image of h_t in R_{a,b}. Assume that P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)) belongs to Z[q]. Then the sequence bar h_{r+a+1}, bar h_{r+a+2}, ..., bar h_{r+b} is regular in R_{a,b}; explicitly, bar h_{r+a+1} is not a zero-divisor in R_{a,b}, for each integer t with a + 2 <= t <= b the image of bar h_{r+t} in R_{a,b}/(bar h_{r+a+1},...,bar h_{r+t-1}) is not a zero-divisor, and the final quotient is not the zero ring.
